evidence.note: CONFIRMED: git for-each-ref %(ahead-behind:...) ends its atom at the first ")" — `git for-each-ref "--format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:rel)x)" refs/heads` exits 128 "fatal: failed to find rel\" and returns nothing. Probe refute-or-confirm: `git rev-parse "rel)x^{commit}"` yields a 40-hex object id with no atom-terminating char, and `git for-each-ref "--format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:<sha>)" refs/heads` returns the correct ahead/behind counts in one call. Regression test test_a_base_branch_with_a_paren_keeps_the_batched_ahead_counts failed on the unfixed code (aheads == {}) and passed after resolving the base to a commit.

Fix follows the adapters rule (all git through ddflow/adapters/git.run single layer), r-derived-cache-bounded (no new state), r-adapters (change in the single git adapter), and r-gemini-key-load for the review step. No rule conflicts; the base-branch resolve-to-commit approach is a minimal change to branch_tip_aheads.

Implemented in ddflow/adapters/git.py branch_tip_aheads: resolve base to a commit via rev-parse --verify --quiet base^{commit} and interpolate the object id into %(ahead-behind:...) so a ) in the branch name can no longer terminate the atom and silently lose the batched for-each-ref. Regression test written first and shown to fail on unfixed code (aheads == {}), passing after the fix. ruff format/check clean on both touched files.
